fields.value: The paper frames robot gaze as a bodily action for displaying the order of service provision and acknowledging the next person waiting for service.

quotes.text: An ethnographic study we conducted at an elderly care center revealed that the gaze and bodily actions of care workers can serve this function.
When an elderly person requested assistance, the gaze projected a request for the service seeker to wait while the care worker finished attending to the current person.

fields.value: Gaze acknowledges and identifies the next service recipient, projects the service order, and signals that the next person should wait while the current service is completed.

quotes.text: In other words, the nurse successfully projects the order to the visitors by only turning her gaze.
Function 4 Display the person who is going to be served next.
Function 5 Display the meaning "please wait until service provision to the current user isfinished" to the next user.

fields.value: Gaze led participants to lower their hands after requesting service, which the authors interpret as recognizing the acknowledgement/order and accepting that they would be served next. Adding a nod after gaze reduced hand-lowering and may have confused participants by suggesting immediate service.

quotes.text: When the robot turned its gaze towards them (pattern 3), 80% of the participants lowered their hands.
This suggests that compound gestures may have unexpected effects.
In other words, participants may have kept their hands up because the robot projected it would come to them immediately but then proceeded to serve the first person beforehand.

fields.value: The mobile robot stopped its torso when another user raised a hand and turned its head toward that user; tested gestures also included raising a hand and nodding, alone and in combinations. The paper does not state that gaze or gestures were selected autonomously, or describe a gaze-detection model/control architecture.

fields.value: Anthropomorphic mobile robot built on a Segway platform, with eight upper-body joints for human-like arm movement and a pan-tilt head; it carried tea and snacks.

quotes.text: To test our theory, we developed an anthropomorphic mobile robot system able to circulate among multiple people.
We adapted a Segway mobile robot (RMP50 by Segway Japan) as the mobile platform.
In the upper body 8 joints were installed to enable the robot to move its arms in a way similar to humans.

fields.value: The paper reports that gaze was performed by turning the robot's head, and that gaze alone was more effective than some hand/nod gestures. It does not explicitly analyze how embodiment shaped the study or effects.

In contrast, the robot raising a hand and nodding (pattern 4) proved relatively less effective than the gaze.

fields.value: The authors studied how a care robot could use gaze and bodily gestures to show who would receive service next in a multiparty tea-serving scenario. Participants responded to gaze by lowering their raised hands, while gaze followed by a nod sometimes suggested immediate service and produced more persistent hand-raising.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper describes gaze as a cue for service order and waiting, tests its effects on hand-raising behavior, and reports the robot's gestures, sensing components, and physical platform. It does not directly examine how embodiment influences the study or effects.
